title: Microsoft 365 Copilot app: return to recently used SharePoint agents
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, existing controls, licensing context and retirement dates are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting older guidance about blocking and reconcile the checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans direct access to most recently used SharePoint agents in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
claims.quote: With this new feature, you can quickly return to your most recently used SharePoint agents directly in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.

claims.claim: The planned experience does not require navigating to the SharePoint site first.
claims.quote: Use SharePoint agents seamlessly without navigating to the SharePoint site.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the default state of the recently used SharePoint agents list.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Microsoft 365 Copilot app recently used agents list default enable disable admin controls account populate roadmap 482601. Read manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint, upgrade-sharepoint-agents and agent-settings; none states this list's default.

claims.claim: No feature-specific control over the recently used list is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Copilot admin SharePoint recently used agents list settings API PowerShell. Read agent-settings, Package Management API overview, package block and restricted-content-discovery; these document general controls, not a control specific to the list.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe the recently used list feature itself at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "482601"; "most recently used SharePoint agents"; "SharePoint agents" "recently" "Copilot". Read manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint and upgrade-sharepoint-agents; search excerpts describe other SharePoint agent changes, not this list.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explained how this roadmap item relates to the .agent upgrade.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents recently used Copilot app licensing billing meter upgrade .agent March 2027; "482601". Read upgrade-sharepoint-agents and manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint; they explain the upgrade and app Home integration, not its relation to this item.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not identified the account or component that populates the recently used list.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Microsoft 365 Copilot app recently used agents list default enable disable admin controls account populate roadmap 482601. Read manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint and upgrade-sharepoint-agents; neither describes list population.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether blocking an agent hides it from the recently used Copilot app list is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Copilot app recently used list block visibility administrator role. Read agent-actions, manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint and package block; these describe blocking usage but do not specify visibility in the recently used list.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters
claims.claim: The roadmap describes returning to agents and mentions no new actions, autonomy or changes to existing agent behaviour.
claims.quote: Use SharePoint agents seamlessly without navigating to the SharePoint site. With this new feature, you can quickly return to your most recently used SharePoint agents directly in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.

claims.claim: The existing SharePoint agent experience uses .agent files.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint are represented as .agent files.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Permissions on the .agent file determine who can access or edit that agent.
claims.quote: The permissions on the `.agent` file determine who can access or edit the agent.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents use SharePoint sites, pages and document libraries as knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint use SharePoint sites, pages, and document libraries as knowledge sources to respond to the user.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SharePoint agents respond based on users' existing data access permissions, like Copilot in other Microsoft 365 apps.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint access your organization's data the same way Copilot in other Microsoft 365 apps does, responding to users based on their access permissions to the data.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Users with a Microsoft Copilot licence can use SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: Currently, users with a Microsoft Copilot license can use the agents.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Administrators can control SharePoint agent access through Copilot licence assignment.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing can provide access to SharePoint agents for users without a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: For users who aren't assigned with a Microsoft Copilot license, you can control user access to agents through pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, reflecting licensed and pay-as-you-go access to SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment. Or, if your organization has the pay-as-you-go billing set up, you can control who can access agents through the security groups assigned to the billing policy.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no licence requirement specific to the recently used list feature.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents recently used Copilot app licensing billing meter upgrade .agent March 2027. Read manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint, sharepoint-agents-azure-billing and microsoft-365-copilot-licensing; none names a licence specific to the list.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no charge or meter specific to this list feature.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents recently used Copilot app licensing billing meter upgrade .agent March 2027. Read sharepoint-agents-azure-billing and upgrade-sharepoint-agents; the billing text covers agent use, not a charge for reopening agents from a recent list.

claims.claim: Whether this list feature changes existing SharePoint agent charges is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents recently used Copilot app licensing billing meter upgrade .agent March 2027. Read sharepoint-agents-azure-billing and upgrade-sharepoint-agents; neither attributes a billing change to the recently used list.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents generally do not require activation.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint don't require activation.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Existing .agent agents continue working in SharePoint, Teams and the Copilot app until the end of March 2027.
claims.quote: Existing agents in the .agent file format will continue to work across SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, and the Copilot app until the end of March 2027.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: .agent files stop responding after March 2027.
claims.quote: After March 2027, .agent files will stop responding and you will have to upgrade to continue using them.

claims.claim: Starting in mid-November 2026, SharePoint and OneDrive agents are created with Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder.
claims.quote: Starting in mid-November 2026, you'll use Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder to create agents for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: The new creation experience no longer saves a .agent file in SharePoint or OneDrive.
claims.quote: However, creating an agent no longer saves a .agent file in SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An agent can be blocked through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **All agents**. In the **All agents** page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select **Block** or **Unblock**.
claims.fix: Keep the path, but add: 'The current agent-actions page documents Block; the December 23, 2025 release notes instead describe replacing block/unblock with delete.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/previous-year-release-notes#december-23,-2025 alongside the existing source.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking an agent created using SharePoint affects only its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The block API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is enabled through SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand **Sites** and select **Active sites**. Select the site you want to configure. Open the **Settings** tab, and then turn **Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot** on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery on a site.
claims.quote:
### Use PowerShell
Open PowerShell as an administrator and run the following command:
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits site content discovery in organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery removes site AI entry points, including the Agent icon and agent creation features.
claims.quote: Once you flag a site with restricted content discovery, users can't see the Agent icon on the global header of the site. Therefore, they don't have access to use the ready-made agent, create new agents, or add content from that site to any other agents.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery leaves site permissions and existing direct access unchanged.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires the organization to be licensed for Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license. Restricted Content Discovery is intended for Microsoft Copilot deployment and governance scenarios.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires SharePoint Advanced Management to be available.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Tenant admins and AI admins can manage and block SharePoint agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Tenant admins and AI admins can manage actively used agents in SharePoint in the Microsoft 365 admin center

claims.claim: The cited SharePoint agent billing table lists a generative answer at 2 messages.
claims.quote: | Generative answer | 2 messages | No charge | 2 messages |

claims.claim: The cited SharePoint agent billing table lists tenant graph grounding at 10 messages.
claims.quote: | Tenant graph grounding for messages | 10 messages | No charge | 10 messages |

claims.claim: SharePoint agent usage charges appear under the Copilot Studio meter on the invoice.
claims.quote: Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice.

claims.claim: Interactive use by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users in Microsoft 365 apps and services is included at no extra cost.
claims.quote: Interactive use of generative answers, tenant graph grounding and agent actions by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users, in Microsoft 365 apps and services, are included at no extra cost.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot licence details page in Microsoft 365 admin center exposes the per-user Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint service plan.
claims.quote: Under the license details page for Microsoft Copilot on the Microsoft 365 admin center, admins can turn 'Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint' on or off on a per-user basis.

claims.claim: Turning off Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint also disables Copilot in OneDrive for that user.
claims.quote: However, this change also disables Copilot in OneDrive and on the SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.

claims.claim: Turning off Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint also disables SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.
claims.quote: However, this change also disables Copilot in OneDrive and on the SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.

claims.claim: Learn documents licence or pay-as-you-go entitlement, per-agent blocking and per-site Restricted Content Discovery as ways to limit SharePoint agent access.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment. ... Control user access through pay-as-you-go billing ... Turn off agents on sites with restricted content discovery ... Block agents from being used in Copilot Chat

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review file permissions, licence assignment and billing-policy connections, but those controls have no table rows.
claims.quote: Before rollout: 'Review which sites hold .agent files and which users can open them'; 'Check who holds a Microsoft Copilot licence, and whether a pay-as-you-go billing policy is connected'. The table contains only agent blocking and Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.fix: The first and third Before rollout bullets name controls missing from the table. Remove those two checklist bullets to reconcile the checklist with the existing table; do not add control rows in this correction.
